email.subject1: a signal play for Smith Micro
email.body1:
Beth, saw Smith Micro launched SafePath 8 with AI social media intelligence and an enhanced SafePath OS for kids phones.

A platform refresh like that usually opens more in-market carriers and operators than a new-business team can cover worldwide, and that is where deals slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Smith Micro off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Beth, quick follow-up for Smith Micro.

With a worldwide remit, your team can only personally touch so many carrier and operator accounts, so the best-fit ones get a generic or late touch. Tightening emails to 75-100 words alone tends to lift responses about 67%, and most teams never hit that at scale.

I had our AI SDR draft 3 personalized emails to your top 3 target accounts. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through them?
email.body3:
Beth, last bit of proof for Smith Micro.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Smith Micro's reply rate likely compares to other enterprise software teams. Want to grab time so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Beth, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling worldwide new-business coverage without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A platform launch is its own kind of busy, and I know timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your new-business motion? I'll tailor it to Smith Micro either way.
